title: An Integrated Flood‐Road‐Network Modeling Approach for Assessing the Impacts of Urban Storms on Road‐Network Performance
content:
Abstract

Urban pluvial flooding increasingly disrupts road transportation systems, posing growing risks to urban functionality and societal well-being. Although previous studies have coupled hydrological models with transportation analysis to assess flood impacts, they commonly represent road functionality in binary terms (i.e., passable or closed) and inadequately account for functional heterogeneity among road segments. This study presents a novel integrated modeling approach that dynamically couples a hydrologic-hydrodynamic model with a weighted road network analysis model to quantify flood-induced transportation disruption. By explicitly linking inundation depth to flood-constrained operating speed at the road-segment scale and weighted network efficiency at the system scale, the approach enables high-resolution, time-varying assessment of flood-constrained road-network serviceability. Data limitations in drainage network representation and model validation are addressed through a design-based drainage network inference module and a crowdsourcing-based inundation data-extraction module. Scenario-based experiments spanning single-peak storms with varying return periods, durations, and peaking times show that road-network efficiency dynamics are controlled primarily by storm duration and peaking time, whereas return period determines the magnitude of maximum efficiency loss. The road network is particularly vulnerable to front-loaded, long-duration storms with large return periods, which cause abrupt efficiency declines and delayed recovery. Further analysis identifies the inundation-induced failure of geographically critical road segments as a key mechanism underlying sudden losses of network connectivity. Overall, this integrated approach advances process-based understanding of flood-induced transportation disruption and provides actionable insights for enhancing road network resilience and supporting emergency traffic management under extreme urban floods.
